the correlations of FDT within a classification are greater than those between the 2 classifications, and that correlations of fatty acids within a classification are also greater than those between classifications.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the correlations of FDT and fatty acids within the same group are much stronger than those between groups.
the amount of adipose tissue is positively correlated with the proportions of SFA or MUFA, whereas the amount of IMF is more related to the proportions of neutral or healthy fatty acid.
increasing the IMF of LM is a better strategy for pork producers to improve pork quality than reducing the amount of adipose tissue in pigs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to increase the proportion of some neutral or beneficial fatty acids in pork without increasing fatness, and this may be achieved by selecting for greater LM IMF.
it is possible to increase the amount of healthy fatty acids in pork by selecting for increased IMF, without reducing the amount of adipose tissue.
the fatty acid composition in adipose tissues and LM can be manipulated independently by altering FDT.
